clue.text: Run campaign supporting heathen on 'loony' side

indicators.note: a loony thing is crazy and disordered, so the next word's letters are scrambled

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a pagan is a heathen
the letters of side rearranged

explanation.surface: A political activist backs an unbeliever who stands on the lunatic fringe.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagandise is to spread persuasive material, which amounts to running a campaign for a cause.

clue.text: Transfer soldier to be handler of correspondence

parts.note: to post someone is to transfer them to a new station
a man is a private soldier, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A soldier is reassigned to work in the mail room.
explanation.definitionFit: A postman carries and delivers letters, so he deals with people's mail every working day.

clue.text: Times said to be shared by you and me

indicators.note: said tells us to go by how the word for times is pronounced, not how it is spelt

parts.note: hours are measures of time, and with a dropped H the word is pronounced like the possessive

explanation.surface: Good times are something two people have in common.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun describes what belongs jointly to the speaker and the person addressed.

clue.text: Burning some garden trash

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A bonfire of garden refuse is burning away.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent comes from the Latin for blazing, and still means burning, both literally and of passionate feeling.

clue.text: Arrogance over journey to crude landing-place

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first word's letters sit above the next ones

parts.note: putting on airs is behaving arrogantly
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A haughty traveller sets off for a rough landing ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a basic runway without terminal buildings, a rough field where small aircraft touch down.

clue.text: I toil sadly, with devil going round wrecking

indicators.note: going round means one word encircles the other letters

parts.note: a demon is a devil

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone badly wrong, so the preceding letters are put out of order

parts.note: the letters of I and toil rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone labouring unhappily while a devil prowls about causing havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: Sadly reads as the toiler's mood, but it scrambles I and toil; the devil then wraps round that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Demolition is the act of tearing down a building, so it is the wrecking of a structure.

clue.text: After daylight, hurry to area of warm climate

indicators.note: after places the second word's letters following the first word's

parts.note: sun is daylight, as in sitting in the sun
to belt along is to hurry

explanation.surface: When the morning comes, rush off somewhere hot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sunbelt is the band of southern US states with a warm climate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunbelt names the southern and southwestern United States, a region known for long, hot summers.

clue.text: Flying at beer rashly? Walk home to avoid this

indicators.note: flying suggests letters scattered through the air and landing in a new order

parts.note: the twelve letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker charging recklessly at the beer is advised to leave the car behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Rashly looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; Flying does the work. Walking home avoids the police roadside alcohol test.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathalyser is the device police use to test drivers for alcohol, which a pedestrian never faces.

clue.text: Warm tint revolted socialist

parts.note: to rise up is to revolt, past tense rose
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A left-winger with a rosy complexion stages an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose-red is a warm pinkish red shade, the colour of a red rose.

clue.text: Can more agonising produce novel, say?

indicators.note: agonising suggests letters writhing in torment and twisting into another order

parts.note: the seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Can a writer's further anguish yield a new book?
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like an anagram signal meaning new, but here it is the book, and say marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a kind of novel, a love story, so a novel is one instance of it.

clue.text: Go in quietly on the way up — that's resourceful

parts.note: to enter is to go in
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly
something rising is on its way up

explanation.surface: Slipping in silently as your career climbs shows initiative.
explanation.walkthrough: On the way up looks like a reversal signal in a down clue, but it simply means rising.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprising person shows initiative and finds ways to get things done, the same as being resourceful.

clue.text: Warriors in Tartar mythology

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Fighters featured in the legends of the Tartar peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a body of soldiers, a collective of fighting men.

clue.text: HP payment left me stuck in a flash

indicators.note: stuck in means the preceding letters are wedged inside another word

parts.note: in a flash means in an instant
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hire-purchase bill landed on me suddenly.
explanation.walkthrough: HP is hire purchase, the British term for buying goods on credit in regular payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Hire purchase is paid off in instalments, regular part-payments of the total price.

clue.text: Nutcase showing intellect after chat

indicators.note: after puts the first word's letters following the second word's

parts.note: crack, or craic, is lively talk
brain stands for intellect

explanation.surface: A madman proves to be clever after a conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: Crack in the sense of chat or banter is Irish and Northern English, also spelt craic.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackbrain is an eccentric or crazy person, the same as a nutcase.

clue.text: Suspended most of grain for starving

indicators.note: most of means the word is used short of its final letter

parts.note: something suspended is hung
rye is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A sack of grain hangs out of reach of the hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone starving badly wants food, which is the everyday sense of hungry.

clue.text: Tyrant who puts his thoughts on record

definitions.text: who puts his thoughts on record
definitions.meaning: second meaning: one who dictates letters or notes to be recorded

explanation.surface: An autocrat who insists on his opinions being written down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an absolute ruler and, literally, a person who dictates words for someone else to take down.

clue.text: Where rep stood, wretched

indicators.note: wretched means in a sorry state, so the letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: the eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: The miserable spot where a travelling salesman waited.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder doubles as part of the definition: a rep, a travelling salesman, waits on the step at the front door.
explanation.definitionFit: A door-to-door salesman stands on the doorstep at each house while making a pitch.

clue.text: Famous essayist joins hack for meat dish

parts.note: Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia
to hack is to chop

explanation.surface: A celebrated essayist teams up with a jobbing writer over dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Hack looks like a journalist to go with the essayist, but here it is the verb to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb chop is a cut of lamb with the rib bone, cooked and served as a dish.

clue.text: Someone making prototypes crumble away

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who makes moulds or shapes models

explanation.surface: A model-maker's designs fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a maker of moulds and a verb for slowly decaying into dust.

clue.text: Domestic animal giving us more trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters are stirred up and disturbed into a new order

parts.note: the six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A pet that causes us extra bother.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouser is a cat kept to catch mice, a household pet.

clue.text: Drink causing brawl on outskirts of Paisley

parts.note: a scrum is a disorderly scuffle

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges of a town, so only the word's outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the town

explanation.surface: Drinking leads to a fight on the edge of a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Paisley is a town near Glasgow; scrumpy is rough farmhouse cider from the West of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumpy is a strong, cloudy cider, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Ass depicted in Iron-Age relics

indicators.note: depicted in means the letters are shown inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A donkey shown on ancient artefacts.
explanation.definitionFit: The onager is a wild ass of central Asia, a relative of the donkey.

clue.text: Unconscious sleeper's head moving heavily

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word it is attached to

parts.note: first letter of sleeper
lumbering is moving in a clumsy, heavy way

explanation.surface: A drowsy person nods off, head lolling heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slumbering is asleep and so not conscious of the world.

clue.text: Satirise jingoist carrying flag

indicators.note: carrying means the word holds the letters inside itself

parts.note: the letters sit inside the word

explanation.surface: Mock the flag-waving patriot.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag looks like a national banner to go with jingoist, but it is the yellow flag, a wild iris.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild iris, and flag is an old name for irises generally.

clue.text: Blue, like this clue

explanation.definitionFit: The word means feeling low, and it also names the direction this very entry runs in the grid.

clue.text: Make new plan of revolutionary floating structure

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary communist
a raft is a flat floating platform

explanation.surface: A rebel designs a new kind of floating platform.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary looks like a reversal signal, but it gives a word for a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraft is to write a fresh version of a document or scheme, drawing up a revised plan.

clue.text: Old-time mate — excellent fellow

parts.note: good means excellent
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A trusted old companion who is a fine chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodman is an archaic term for a husband or the master of a household, a spouse in old usage.

clue.text: Picture said to typify open government

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a photographic slide viewed by light passing through it
second meaning: the quality of being open to public scrutiny

explanation.surface: An image held up as the model of open politics.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a slide for a projector, and also openness, the quality claimed by accountable administrations.
